title: Programming Language Concepts
summary: The ideas every language makes choices about: compilation, typing, memory, numbers, strings and concurrency. Memory management is the threshold: once you see who frees memory and when, the differences between C, Java, Python and Rust stop being folklore.
sources: Abelson & Sussman: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
Goldberg: What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic (1991)
Klabnik & Nichols: The Rust Programming Language

nodes.label: Compiled vs Interpreted
nodes.summary: Ahead-of-time compilation, interpretation, bytecode and just-in-time compilers.
nodes.outcome: Explain how a given language turns source into running code.
nodes.check: What is the main difference between an ahead-of-time compiled language and an interpreted one?
nodes.answer: A compiler translates the whole program to machine code before it runs; an interpreter executes it statement by statement at run time (many languages mix both with bytecode and a JIT).

nodes.label: Static vs Dynamic Typing
nodes.summary: Types checked before running (static) or while running (dynamic), and how strictly values are converted.
nodes.outcome: Classify languages by static/dynamic and strong/weak typing.
nodes.check: When are type errors caught in a statically typed language?
nodes.answer: At compile time, before the program runs.

nodes.label: "Dynamic typing means weak typing"
nodes.summary: Python is dynamic yet strongly typed; JavaScript is dynamic and coerces freely. Two separate axes.
nodes.check: Python is dynamically typed. Is '1' + 1 allowed in Python?
nodes.answer: No: it raises a TypeError. Python is dynamic but strongly typed; it's JavaScript that coerces.

nodes.label: Memory Management: Manual, GC, Ownership
nodes.summary: Who frees memory, and when: the programmer (C), a garbage collector (Java, Python, Go) or the compiler's ownership rules (Rust).
nodes.outcome: Compare the costs and failure modes of each memory strategy.
nodes.check: Name the three main approaches to freeing memory, with a language for each.
nodes.answer: Manual management (C), garbage collection (Java, Python, Go) and ownership with borrowing (Rust).

nodes.label: Paradigms
nodes.summary: Imperative, object-oriented, functional and logic programming, and languages that mix them.
nodes.outcome: Solve one problem in two paradigms and compare.
nodes.check: Which paradigm treats computation as evaluating functions without changing state?

nodes.label: Numbers: Integer Division & Overflow
nodes.summary: Integer division, remainders of negative numbers and overflow all differ between languages.
nodes.outcome: Predict integer arithmetic results across languages.
nodes.check: In C and Java, what is 7 / 2 when both operands are integers?

nodes.label: Floating Point
nodes.summary: IEEE 754 binary floats: fast, approximate, and full of surprises.
nodes.outcome: Explain and avoid floating-point comparison bugs.
nodes.check: Why is 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 false in most languages?
nodes.answer: 0.1 and 0.2 have no exact binary representation, so the sum is 0.30000000000000004.

nodes.label: "Computers do decimal arithmetic exactly"
nodes.summary: Binary floats can't represent most decimal fractions; money needs integers or decimal types.
nodes.outcome: Choose a correct representation for money.
nodes.check: Should you store money as a binary floating-point number?
nodes.answer: No: use integers (cents) or a decimal type, because binary floats can't represent many decimal fractions exactly.

nodes.label: Strings & Unicode
nodes.summary: Bytes, code units, code points and grapheme clusters: four different 'lengths'.
nodes.outcome: Handle text correctly in at least two languages.
nodes.check: Why can the 'length' of '👍🏽' differ between languages?
nodes.answer: Some count bytes, some UTF-16 code units, some code points and some grapheme clusters.

nodes.label: Concurrency Models
nodes.summary: Threads and locks, async/await, channels (Go) and actors (Erlang).
nodes.outcome: Choose a concurrency model for a workload.
nodes.check: How does Go's approach to concurrency differ from shared-memory threads with locks?
nodes.answer: Goroutines communicate over channels ('share memory by communicating') instead of sharing state guarded by locks.

nodes.label: Package Managers & Toolchains
nodes.summary: npm, pip, Cargo, Maven: dependency resolution, lockfiles and reproducible builds.
nodes.outcome: Set up a reproducible project in a new language.
nodes.check: What does a lockfile (package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock) guarantee?
nodes.answer: Reproducible installs: every install resolves the exact same dependency versions.

nodes.label: Choosing a Language
nodes.summary: Runtime, ecosystem, team and problem domain matter more than syntax.
nodes.outcome: Justify a language choice for a project with an ADR.
nodes.check: Why is C still the default for microcontroller firmware?
nodes.answer: Tiny runtime, direct hardware access, predictable performance and compilers for every chip.
